question: Should maintainers accept this new Codex sandbox diagnostic surface after a rebase, or require a narrower/redaction-proven port first?
rationale: The code is useful but exposes a new sandbox failure-data channel and scans Codex rollout files, and the external PR has no real runtime proof on the conflicting current-main path.

options.title: Require rebase and live proof
options.body: Port onto current main, keep the diagnostic payload bounded/redacted, and add redacted terminal or log proof from a real apply_patch failure before merge.

options.title: Accept source-only diagnostics
options.body: Proceed after conflict resolution based on tests and source inspection, accepting the residual redaction and runtime-scan risk.

options.title: Replace with maintainer port
options.body: Pause or close this branch if the current-main conflict makes a narrow maintainer-authored diagnostic port cheaper than preserving the submitted diff.

recommendation.title: Require rebase and live proof
recommendation.body: Port onto current main, keep the diagnostic payload bounded/redacted, and add redacted terminal or log proof from a real apply_patch failure before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The current-main conflict is in the Codex turn-routing work from #101376, which steipete authored and merged.
